headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; no direct isolation evidence is provided.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can orchestrate files/APIs and Transformers reads files/stdin and can run subprocesses, so a shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content influence downstream parsing. No direct shared-channel evidence is provided, so I avoid high. The pairwise pathway is plausible from both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or copied files, prompt-like content in Airflow outputs can reach Transformers inputs.
IF Transformers treats file or stdin content as trusted instructions, injected text can steer processing.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories and mount points.
Add a manual review step before Transformers consumes Airflow-generated files.
Strip instruction-like text from exchanged artifacts.
Use allowlisted file formats only.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and Transformers can read files and send requests to Hugging Face Hub or serve endpoints. If sensitive data enters Airflow and is handed to Transformers, either agent can move it across process or network boundaries. No evidence shows actual sensitive classes, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in a shared workspace, Transformers can read them and potentially transmit them via networked APIs.
IF Airflow tasks pass secrets or regulated data into files, those contents can be exposed through downstream processing.
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of shared directories.
Disable outbound network for the Transformers runtime when processing sensitive data.
Use separate service accounts and credentials.
Review logs for accidental payload capture.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on handoff paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is an automation/orchestration system and Transformers can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. If both operate on the same directory or environment, concurrent writes or package changes can corrupt state or overwrite artifacts. The profiles do not show locking or isolation, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same working directory, file corruption or overwrite is possible.
IF Transformers installs packages in the same environment Airflow uses, dependency drift can break pipelines.
mitigations: Use separate working directories.
Pin and isolate Python environments.
Run only one writer per directory at a time.
Snapshot artifacts before downstream mutation.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate pipeline outputs that Transformers may consume as files or stdin, and Transformers can then transform or act on them without any documented verification step. That creates a default path where an upstream mistake propagates into downstream outputs or actions. Because the pair lacks explicit validation controls, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Airflow-produced artifacts are fed directly into Transformers, upstream errors can cascade into downstream outputs.
IF downstream automation trusts model output without checks, incorrect content can be propagated.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require schema checks on all exchanged artifacts.
Compare outputs against source data before acting.
Limit Transformers to read-only analysis for critical flows.
requires-engineering: add automated regression tests for handoff formats.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not declare regulated data classes, residency, or certifications. Airflow touches no data classes and Transformers lists generic multimodal types, so there is no concrete compliance mismatch shown. I cite both profiles because the assessment is pairwise, but the evidence supports only a low-risk gap.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into the shared workflow, compliance review is required.
IF one agent is deployed under stricter residency or retention rules than the other, policy mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Document data classes handled by each agent.
Confirm retention settings for logs and artifacts.
Keep regulated data out of the pair until reviewed.
Assign separate compliance owners.
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls end-to-end.
